questions.question: The Bharatiya Vayuyan Vidheyak, 2024, replaces which of the following Acts?

• The Aircraft Act, 1934 provided the legal framework for the regulation of civil aviation, including aircraft manufacturing, maintenance, and airworthiness.
 
• The Act was considered outdated and insufficient for addressing the modern challenges of aviation safety, technology, and infrastructure.
 
• The new Bharatiya Vayuyan Vidheyak, 2024 aims to modernize the regulatory framework for civil aviation in line with international standards and advancements.
 
• This new legislation will streamline aviation governance and ensure compliance with global aviation protocols established by organizations like ICAO (International Civil Aviation Organization).

• It authorized the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) to regulate civil aviation activities in India.
 
• The Act contained provisions for the investigation of aircraft accidents and penalties for regulatory violations.
 
 
 
• **International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO):**
 
 
• An agency of the United Nations responsible for setting global aviation safety standards.
 
• India is a member of ICAO and adheres to its guidelines for civil aviation operations.
 
 
 
• **DGCA:**
 
 
• The Directorate General of Civil Aviation is India’s regulatory body for civil aviation.
 
• It oversees aircraft certification, pilot licensing, air traffic management, and aviation safety standards.

• The Bharatiya Vayuyan Vidheyak, 2024 reflects the growing demand for enhanced safety, technology integration, and sustainable practices in aviation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about the Animal Birth Control Rules, 2023, notified by the Central Government in April 2023?

options.text: State governments can choose any government veterinary hospital to implement the Animal Birth Control programme.

questions.solution:

• It works to ensure that animals are treated humanely and to prevent cruelty to animals.
 
• AWBI recognizes and authorizes organizations to conduct ABC programmes, ensuring they follow the prescribed guidelines.

questions.question: In which year was the 'Bharatiya Sakshya Bill' passed in India?

The correct answer is __**2023**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bharatiya Sakshya Bill was passed by the Indian Parliament in the year **2023**.
 
• This bill is significant as it seeks to revamp the **evidence law in India**.
 
• The bill aims to replace the colonial-era **Indian Evidence Act of 1872**.
 
• The new legislation intends to modernize the judicial process by incorporating **technological advancements** and addressing contemporary legal challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Evidence Act, 1872**

 
 
• The Indian Evidence Act was a comprehensive set of rules and guidelines that governed the admissibility of evidence in Indian courts.
 
• It was enacted during the British colonial rule and has been a cornerstone of the Indian judicial system for over a century.
 
• The act categorized evidence into various types such as oral, documentary, primary, and secondary evidence.
 
• The act also laid down the burden of proof and standards of proof required in different legal contexts.
 
 
 
• **Technological Advancements in Law**
 
 
• The new Bharatiya Sakshya Bill aims to integrate modern technology into the legal process.
 
• It includes provisions for the admissibility of digital evidence.
 
• It also addresses the need for electronic records and digital signatures to be legally recognized.
